items.title: INFO 521: Introduction to Machine Learning
items.text:
Build a reproducible data-cleaning and exploratory-analysis notebook, then fit a small CPU model with held-out validation. Explain missingness, leakage, uncertainty and data provenance.

Inputs: Generate a synthetic civic-service dataset with no real residents; keep core CSV inputs below 250 MB and test peak memory against the awarded workspace. Real/public datasets require a rights and data-classification check.

Environment: Requested: Python, JupyterLab, pandas, scikit-learn, matplotlib and an approved reproducible package manifest; R/RStudio only if the course requires it.

Outputs and acceptance
  • Run the same environment from a browser and from the CPU fallback.
  • Produce a reproducible notebook with an environment manifest and checksummed inputs.
  • Evaluate a small model without requiring a GPU or a paid student account.

Run the whole assignment from a fresh student workspace; require execution without out-of-memory errors at the approved spec, reproducible key outputs and a complete exported submission.

items.title: LIS 671: Digital Curation and Digital Preservation
items.text:
Audit a collection catalog, normalize names/dates/identifiers, document a metadata crosswalk, query an embedded catalog database and export a preservation-ready package with README, schema, provenance and checksums.

Inputs: Use a synthetic 10,000–100,000-record collection catalog with Dublin Core-style fields. Add public/licensed records only after rights review; exclude patron, circulation, donor and restricted collection records.

Environment: Requested: JupyterLab/Python, CSV/JSON/XML parsing and embedded SQLite; optional MARC parsing packages after approval. OpenRefine or other hosted applications require a separate provider fit check.

Outputs and acceptance
  • Explain how transformations change discoverability and preserve provenance.
  • Validate a metadata crosswalk and query structured collection records.
  • Export usable CSV/JSON/XML records and describe a suitable repository/retention route.

Execute the complete workflow in a fresh workspace; validate schema, record counts, identifiers and query results; reopen the exported package using the fallback environment.

items.title: Our focus
items.text:
AI research and teaching depend on infrastructure, tools, data and people. The group considers hardware, software, data, cloud services, research software engineers (RSEs), technical support, collaboration and shared infrastructure across the college and university.

Growing demand, rising costs and uncertain funding make access and sustainable support important planning questions. Our focus is the needs, capabilities and perspectives of Information Science faculty and students.

Compare technologies, shared services, partnerships, staffing models and innovation.

items.title: Before required classroom use
items.text:
Supporting compute pilot. These DS/MLIS proposals retain their own $0 cash and Greg’s ten-hour weekly envelope. They are not college-wide capacity findings or the working group’s selected solution. Return to working-group deliverables →

All 13 admission checks are planned, not run. A working notebook or award alone does not establish classroom readiness. Open a check to see the evidence and stop condition.

1. Operations · scope

Status: Planned — not run

Confirm eligible PI, actual courses/leads, Greg’s ten-hour/week total envelope, separate TA/lead hours, distinct backup and full-term coverage. No cash budget; fund any necessary expenses only from a confirmed eligible grant.

Owner / timing: Greg + course leads / Before request

Evidence: Named owners, realistic hours log, separate support commitments and confirmed grant/allowable-cost evidence if paid resources are needed.

Stop if: Counting ten hours per role, assuming grant award, missing backup, or unfunded necessary spending.

2. Teaching · benchmark

Status: Planned — not run

Complete campus AWS CPU component tests and free-resource GPU benchmarks; retain failures, correctness, measured memory/runtime, checkpoint/export results and workload scope. Reproduce representative GPU work on awarded ACCESS hardware before class.

Owner / timing: Greg (operator) + course leads / Before student canary / request sizing

Evidence: Versioned workload/environment manifest, dataset checksums, dated result rows, actual GPU/account limits and target-resource comparison. No measurements recorded yet.

Stop if: Unmeasured GPU amounts, treating free quota as guaranteed classroom capacity, or assuming benchmark timings transfer unchanged to ACCESS.

3. Access · provider

Status: Planned — not run

Confirm ACCESS CPU/GPU allocation, separate resource exchanges, actual quotas/storage, course dates and project structure; campus AWS stays test-only. If CloudBank is selected, confirm service type, CPU/GPU availability and accounting.

Owner / timing: Allocation lead + selected ACCESS provider / Before request / gate to class

Evidence: Provider response and approved award/resource configuration, recorded privately.

Stop if: Assuming unspecified limits, general broker terms or automatic renewal.

4. Access · accounts

Status: Planned — not run

Every approved student/staff test account authenticates; student A cannot read/write student B files or instructor grading areas; removal/revocation works.

Owner / timing: Operator + course leads / Canary; repeat before week 1

Evidence: Access matrix and dated test results; no passwords or roster identifiers in public reports.

Stop if: Access leakage, shared credentials or unverified removal.

5. Teaching · software

Status: Planned — not run

Both complete representative assignments run on the approved CPU image from fresh workspaces; no paid account or GPU is required. Pin the approved environment and input checksums.

Owner / timing: Each course lead / Canary

Evidence: Clean-run outputs, environment manifest, resource measurements and a known-good baseline.

Stop if: Missing packages, memory failure, unapproved app or required GPU dependency.

6. Access · capacity

Status: Planned — not run

With provider permission, rehearse 80 simultaneous students plus agreed staff use in three representative sessions. Proposed p95 login-to-workspace ≤5 minutes; no unresolved assignment-blocking launch failure.

Owner / timing: Operator + provider / 2–4 weeks before term

Evidence: Dated latency distribution, workspace success count, quota/usage forecast and provider-agreed concurrency.

Stop if: No permission/capacity evidence; peak spec exceeds awarded limits.

7. Teaching · save

Status: Planned — not run

Edit, save, stop/restart and recover a notebook/data package; verify filesystem location and retention. Export and re-import it into the CPU fallback.

Owner / timing: Course leads + TAs / Canary; repeat after image update

Evidence: Saved-file checksums, restart/export receipt and fresh-environment reopen.

Stop if: Student work depends on an unsaved session or cannot be exported.

8. Teaching · grades

Status: Planned — not run

Distribute a versioned assignment, collect it, reconcile all test submissions, preserve student authorship and instructor judgment, and import/export a test grade receipt through the approved LMS workflow. If Classroom 50 is selected, verify Team/Enterprise organization eligibility, permissions, billing controls and an independent export; Codespaces and Actions quotas remain separate.

Owner / timing: Course leads / Before graded use

Evidence: Submission manifest and grade reconciliation results in the approved institutional destination. Classroom 50 canary and quota/fallback records if selected; no additional Codespaces allocation assumed.

Stop if: A leaderboard/auto-score substitutes for the authoritative grade, or a missing receipt goes undetected.

9. Operations · data

Status: Planned — not run

Approve provider and backup data destinations, lawful/appropriate datasets, access roles and retention. Keep grades/rosters in the approved LMS/institutional systems; publish only aggregate results.

Owner / timing: IT/privacy reviewer + Libraries / Before student data

Evidence: Approved data map, rights notes, retention schedule and service/accessibility review.

Stop if: Assuming research storage or this public site is approved for private student records.

10. Teaching · accessibility

Status: Planned — not run

Rehearse keyboard and screen-reader access, readable instructions and equivalent small-data CPU/offline activity; resolve barriers in essential workflows.

Owner / timing: Greg (design coordination) + course leads / Before course admission

Evidence: User/task review and course-lead sign-off, with accommodations and fallback instructions.

Stop if: An essential assessed activity is inaccessible without an equivalent route.

11. Recovery · recovery

Status: Planned — not run

Make independent copies in approved destinations and restore onto a different host/environment. Proposed RPO ≤24 hours and RTO ≤one business day; measure both.

Owner / timing: Primary + backup operators / Before course admission

Evidence: Restore logs, independent file checksums, recovery timing and backup-operator runbook rehearsal.

Stop if: No independent copy or unmeasured recovery; relying only on snapshots or cold archival retrieval.

12. Operations · support

Status: Planned — not run

Publish actual staffed help windows and escalation route; rehearse an outage with CPU/small-data fallback. Proposed first response within one staffed business day; do not promise 24/7 support. Keep actual Greg hours within ten/week across all duties; reduce scope when demand exceeds coverage.

Owner / timing: Owner + TAs + operators / Before week 1; weekly

Evidence: Coverage schedule, ticket routing, outage exercise and fallback delivery proof.

Stop if: Unfunded coverage, unreachable operator or missed class deadline without substitution.

13. Recovery · exit

Status: Planned — not run

Schedule alerts 60/30/14/7 days before expiry; decide continuation at least 30 days before. Rehearse learner/grade export, retention and deletion; verify closure on the approved dates.

Owner / timing: Service owner + course leads + Libraries / Before start; execute near term end

Evidence: End-of-term runbook, sample exports, provider confirmation of exit window and deletion/renewal decision.

Stop if: Relying on grace periods, unconfirmed education extension or archival deposits of private coursework.

items.text: Draft action framework — priorities and endorsement pending. The working group should refine these using the inventory and faculty/student needs, rather than assume a single platform solves the problem.

items.title: Actions the college can pursue
items.text:
1. Maintain a concise resource inventory. Identify an owner role for each entry and a review process. Publish access routes and limitations that resource owners confirm.
  2. Document needs across research and instruction. Use consistent briefs and an agreed university channel; include faculty, students, RSEs and technical staff. Summarize participation and unknowns.
  3. Improve discoverability and reuse. Test clear onboarding, reusable environments, shared documentation and relevant training before expanding infrastructure.
  4. Scope bounded pilots. Match a small activity to a confirmed route and support window. Measure benefit, access, effort and recovery before making it required.

items.title: What changed?
items.text:
GitLab private Free group limits, Bitbucket aggregate storage caps and Google source-hosting onboarding restrictions constrain specific use. GitHub Free still offers unlimited repository counts. Heroku’s free tiers ended; Glitch hosting ended; several free database products closed or shortened their lifetime. These are distinct policies, not evidence that all repository accounts disappeared.

items.title: A practical repair plan
items.text:
1. Inventory code, files, metadata, app runtimes, databases and ownership separately.
  2. Choose a bounded route with an approved fallback; do not assume allocated compute is durable managed hosting.
  3. Keep portable environments, schemas, database dumps and rights-cleared file exports.
  4. Test restore on a second environment. Proposed targets: a 24-hour recovery point and one-business-day recovery; neither is achieved yet.
  5. Export student work, close permissions and use appropriate library archival routes for lasting outputs.

items.title: How to choose
items.text:
1. Define the smallest useful workload, software and outputs.
  2. Match CPU, memory, GPU/VRAM, storage and interactive or batch use.
  3. Check eligibility, permitted data, payment requirements and the whole-term access window.
  4. Measure, test recovery and name support before making it required.

items.title: Supporting compute-pilot sequence
items.text: The separate CPU/GPU pilot stages depend on measurements, resource approval and classroom checks. Those gates do not define the working group’s semester deadlines.

items.title: Run a working session
items.text: Use a short, repeatable review. This is a suggested meeting format, not a scheduled event or an assigned set of roles.

items.title: Before the session
items.text: Choose a deliverable and review its current draft. Bring a public or appropriately shareable resource correction or needs brief. Use the group’s agreed university channel for internal material; the public website does not collect responses.

items.title: Suggested 45-minute agenda
items.text: Minutes Activity Record 0–5 Confirm the decision or question Scope and intended outcome 5–15 Review resources and access Verified facts, owners and unknowns 15–25 Discuss needs and barriers Research/teaching differences and missing perspectives 25–35 Compare promising approaches Evidence, prerequisites and a useful small test 35–45 Agree next steps Action, owner role, dependencies and review point

items.title: After the session
items.text: Update the draft’s date and status. Separate a decision from an open question or suggested action. Record who needs to confirm access, costs, support or permissions; do not list an unconfirmed resource as ready.

items.title: Questions for the group to settle first
items.text:
• Who maintains each deliverable and confirms factual corrections?
  • Which approved university channel will receive needs briefs and internal notes?
  • How will faculty, students and technical staff contribute, and how will missing perspectives be recorded?
  • Who will review the preliminary drafts before early Spring 2027 circulation?
